titulo: Schedule with a gate: the channel runs on its own, you decide
hero_alt: A wall calendar marked with early-morning times and a phone showing an alert message.
lead: The schedule turns the pipeline into a channel: one run a day, at a set time, without you having to remember. But a schedule without a gate means posting the wrong thing faster. In this lesson, you’ll write the timer, decide what happens on a day with no topic, and run a week approving each video until you stop having to reject them.
objetivo: write your channel’s schedule and run a week with manual approval, turning each rejection into a rule.

aprende.t: The three messages: video, no topic, failed
The week with a gate and when to remove it

secoes.sub: Click each block. This is what happens every early morning in a radar.

nos.detalhe: The systemd timer (for your user) starts the run at the scheduled time. For finviral: Monday through Friday at 02:00 for the daily run, Saturday for the weekly run, and Sunday for next week’s run.
Before anything else, the run checks pular.txt. A line with the date and mode skips that run without turning off the schedule: a holiday, a trip, a sensitive topic.
Collection, database, script, review, avatar, and video: lessons 3 to 5 running on their own. If the script has no material, SEM_PAUTA.txt is created and the run ends there.

During the first week, nothing goes live without your approval. Each rejection is recorded with the reason and becomes a rule in regras.md. Only after 3 days in a row without rejecting anything should you consider removing the gate from a step.
Every run ends with a message on Telegram: the video (with the link), “no topic,” or “failed at X.” Silence is never an answer: if nothing arrived, something got stuck before the alert.

secoes.volta: Each rejection becomes a rule; the next run reads it right away
secoes.legenda: Each radar runs at a different time (02:00, 05:00, 08:00) so they don’t compete for the GPU and avatar studio.

secoes.sub: The finviral model, for you to adapt.

texto: 40 to 60 seconds on what the sources published yesterday and the day before.
90 seconds to 2 minutes with a recap of the week. The radars also produce a long 16:9 video, "The week explained," from 5 to 7 minutes.
About 90 seconds on what the sources expect for next week.
Decide in advance what happens on a day with no news: no video, and the message "no story" with the reason. Forcing a video on a slow day is the first step toward publishing the wrong thing.

exemplo.texto: no story: none of the channels published a new video during this period.

secoes.sub: A systemd timer for your user (finviral works this way). Replace <canal> and the script path.

blocos.conteudo:
[Unit]
Description=<canal> — daily at 02:00

[Timer]
OnCalendar=Mon..Fri *-*-* 02:00:00
Persistent=false

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target

[Unit]
Description=<canal> — daily run
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/bin/bash %h/projetos/<canal>/auto/rodar.sh diario
TimeoutStartSec=10h
MemoryMax=60G
Nice=5

systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now <canal>-diario.timer
systemctl --user list-timers '<canal>-*'

# skip one run without disabling the schedule
echo "2026-10-17 diario" >> auto/pular.txt

# minute hour day month day-of-week  command
0 2 * * 1-5  /bin/bash $HOME/projetos/<canal>/auto/rodar.sh diario

abas.html: With Persistent=false, a missed run (the machine is off at 02:00) does not run late when the machine comes back on. For a daily radar, a video about yesterday published in the afternoon is no use.

TimeoutStartSec and MemoryMax are limits: a run that gets stuck is stopped, and one that uses too much memory won’t bring the machine down. A run with no limit that gets stuck at 02:00 is still stuck at 09:00.

secoes.sub: Run it for a week. Interrupt it halfway through, then run it again.

msg.rodando: Each run: collection, source, script, review, and your gate.
msg.parou: Interrupted: the middle run didn’t finish. Next time, it starts over; completed runs aren’t repeated.
msg.retoma: Resumed: anything already approved isn’t done again.
msg.fimfalha: There was no topic on Wednesday: no video, and the bot received "no topic". A slow day doesn’t become a video.

secoes.legenda: Illustrative browser simulation. Wednesday with no topic is intentional, to show that an empty day is a normal result, not an error.

secoes.titulo: Practice: schedule and week with a gate

exercicios.texto: Choose the frequency and write the schedule (systemd timer or cron), including what happens on a day with no topic and where the failure alert goes.
exercicios.pronto: the schedule is written, list-timers (or crontab) shows the next run, and you know what happens on a day with no topic.

exercicios.texto: Run for a week with manual approval before each post. Note what you reject and why; each rejection becomes a rule in regras.md.
exercicios.pronto: you’ve gone 3 days in a row without needing to reject anything. Only then consider removing the gate from a step.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: When is it reasonable to remove the gate from a step?
opcoes: In the first week, to save time.
After 3 days in a row without needing to reject anything.
Never: the gate is required for everything.
When the channel passes one thousand subscribers.
perguntas.explica: E6 requires three days in a row without a rejection. Before then, the gate is still teaching the channel new rules.

perguntas.p: It’s 9 a.m. and you haven’t received anything from the bot. What does that mean?
opcoes: That it was a day with no topic.
That something got stuck before the alert: every run ends with a video, "no topic," or "failed at X."
That the video was posted and there was no need to alert you.
perguntas.explica: Silence is never an answer. A day with no topic sends "no topic"; a failure sends "failed at X." If nothing arrived, check the run.

perguntas.p: Tomorrow is a holiday, and you don’t want a video. What can you do without turning off the schedule?
opcoes: Delete the timer and create it again later.
Put the date and mode in pular.txt.
Let it post and delete it afterward.
perguntas.explica: A line like "2026-10-17 diario" in pular.txt skips only that run.

perguntas.p: Why use Persistent=false on a daily radar timer?
opcoes: So a missed run doesn’t happen late, posting yesterday afternoon’s radar.
perguntas.explica: A daily radar loses its meaning if it runs late. A missed run stays missed; the next one runs on time.
